questions.text: The Keynesian explanation attributes business cycles mainly to fluctuations in:
questions.explanation: Swings in consumption and investment demand drive output fluctuations.

questions.text: A recession is generally characterised by:
questions.explanation: Contraction lowers demand, output and jobs.
questions.source: ICAI Business Economics study material – Unit 5: Business Cycles

questions.text: Which action is most likely for firms in the recovery phase?
options: Increase production and hiring as demand revives
questions.explanation: Revival in demand encourages higher output and employment.
questions.source: ICAI Business Economics study material – Unit 5: Business Cycles

questions.text: Which sequence correctly represents the phases of a business cycle?
questions.explanation: After a trough the economy expands to a peak, then contracts to a new trough.
questions.source: ICAI Business Economics study material – Unit 5: Business Cycles

questions.text: Business cycles are fluctuations in:
options: aggregate economic activity such as output, employment and income
the price of a single commodity
questions.explanation: They concern economy-wide activity.
questions.source: ICAI Business Economics study material – Unit 5: Business Cycles

questions.text: Business cycles are:
questions.explanation: They repeat but vary in duration and intensity.
questions.source: ICAI Business Economics study material – Unit 5: Business Cycles

questions.text: Which of the following typically characterises the expansion/boom phase?
options: Rising output, employment and investment with rising prices
questions.explanation: Growing demand pulls up output, jobs and eventually prices.
questions.source: ICAI Business Economics study material – Unit 5: Business Cycles

questions.text: The lowest point of a business cycle is called the:
questions.explanation: Output and employment are at their lowest before recovery begins.
questions.source: ICAI Business Economics study material – Unit 5: Business Cycles

questions.text: Which of the following is NOT a phase of a business cycle?
questions.explanation: Devaluation is an exchange-rate policy, not a phase.
questions.source: ICAI Business Economics study material – Unit 5: Business Cycles

questions.text: Which of the following is a feature of a trough?
options: Lowest level of output and employment, with idle capacity
Highest level of prices and output
questions.explanation: At the trough, the economy is at its weakest.
questions.source: ICAI Business Economics study material – Unit 5: Business Cycles

questions.text: The highest point of a business cycle is called the:
questions.explanation: At the peak, activity is at its maximum before turning down.
questions.source: ICAI Business Economics study material – Unit 5: Business Cycles

questions.text: A fall in aggregate demand leading firms to cut production and employment signals movement into:
questions.explanation: Falling demand reduces output and jobs.
questions.source: ICAI Business Economics study material – Unit 5: Business Cycles

questions.text: Which statement about a depression is correct?
options: It is the same as the peak
It is a severe and prolonged downturn with very high unemployment and low demand
It is a short-lived mild slowdown
It is a period of full employment
questions.explanation: Depression is the extreme form of contraction.

questions.text: Which of the following is a normative statement?
options: Unemployment fell by one percentage point last year.
The inflation rate rose to 6% last year.
The government should reduce the price of cooking gas to help households.
A rise in income increases the demand for cars.
questions.explanation: Normative statements contain value judgments ("should"). Positive statements can be tested against facts.
questions.chapterName: Nature and Scope of Business Economics
questions.source: ICAI Business Economics study material – Unit 1: Nature and Scope of Business Economics

questions.text: Which of the following falls within the scope of business economics?
options: Demand analysis, cost and production analysis and pricing decisions
questions.explanation: Demand, production/cost and pricing are core areas of business economics.
questions.chapterName: Nature and Scope of Business Economics
questions.source: ICAI Business Economics study material – Unit 1: Nature and Scope of Business Economics

questions.text: A point lying inside the production possibility curve indicates:
options: a level of output that is unattainable
full employment with the best technology
questions.explanation: Points inside the PPC show that resources are idle or inefficiently used; output can rise with no sacrifice of the other good.
questions.chapterName: Nature and Scope of Business Economics
questions.source: ICAI Business Economics study material – Unit 1: Nature and Scope of Business Economics

questions.text: A production possibility curve (PPC) is generally concave to the origin because of:
options: increasing opportunity cost as more of one good is produced
questions.explanation: Resources are not equally suited to all uses, so each extra unit of one good costs ever larger amounts of the other.
questions.chapterName: Nature and Scope of Business Economics
questions.source: ICAI Business Economics study material – Unit 1: Nature and Scope of Business Economics

questions.text: An outward shift of the production possibility curve represents:
questions.explanation: More resources or improved technology expand the economy's productive capacity, shifting the PPC outward.
questions.chapterName: Nature and Scope of Business Economics
questions.source: ICAI Business Economics study material – Unit 1: Nature and Scope of Business Economics

questions.text: The equi-marginal principle states that a limited resource should be allocated among alternative uses so that:
options: each use receives an equal amount of the resource
the entire resource goes to the use with highest average return
marginal returns from every use are equal
total returns from every use are equal
questions.explanation: Shifting resources from low to high marginal return uses continues until marginal returns are equalised.
questions.chapterName: Nature and Scope of Business Economics
questions.source: ICAI Business Economics study material – Unit 1: Nature and Scope of Business Economics

questions.text: According to the marginal principle, a decision-maker should expand an activity as long as:
questions.explanation: Expand while MB > MC; the best level is reached where they are equal.
questions.chapterName: Nature and Scope of Business Economics
questions.source: ICAI Business Economics study material – Unit 1: Nature and Scope of Business Economics

questions.text: The fundamental economic problem of every society arises because:
options: all goods are produced by the private sector
money is not available with households
resources are scarce relative to unlimited human wants
questions.explanation: Scarcity of resources against unlimited wants forces choices about what, how and for whom to produce.
questions.chapterName: Nature and Scope of Business Economics
questions.source: ICAI Business Economics study material – Unit 1: Nature and Scope of Business Economics

questions.text: The discounting (time value) principle is based on the idea that:
options: a rupee received today is worth more than a rupee received in the future
a rupee today is worth the same as a rupee in future
questions.explanation: Because of time value of money, future costs and benefits are discounted to present value.
questions.chapterName: Nature and Scope of Business Economics
questions.source: ICAI Business Economics study material – Unit 1: Nature and Scope of Business Economics

questions.text: Which economist defined economics as "a science which studies human behaviour as a relationship between ends and scarce means which have alternative uses"?
questions.explanation: Robbins' scarcity definition stresses unlimited ends, scarce means and alternative uses, so choice is unavoidable.
questions.chapterName: Nature and Scope of Business Economics
questions.source: ICAI Business Economics study material – Unit 1: Nature and Scope of Business Economics

questions.text: Which of the following is a microeconomic issue?
options: The rate of inflation in the economy
Determination of the price of a single commodity such as wheat
The national income of a country
questions.explanation: Microeconomics studies individual units (consumers, firms, single markets). The others are economy-wide aggregates.
questions.chapterName: Nature and Scope of Business Economics
questions.source: ICAI Business Economics study material – Unit 1: Nature and Scope of Business Economics

questions.text: Which of the following is an economic good?
options: Rainwater falling on an open field
questions.explanation: Economic goods are scarce and have a price and opportunity cost; free gifts of nature are abundant.
questions.chapterName: Nature and Scope of Business Economics
questions.source: ICAI Business Economics study material – Unit 1: Nature and Scope of Business Economics

questions.text: Which feature distinguishes business economics from pure theoretical economics?
options: It ignores the problem of scarcity
It deals only with macro aggregates
It is pragmatic and focuses on solving practical business problems
It is purely descriptive with no analysis
questions.explanation: Business economics is applied and decision-oriented, unlike abstract theory.
questions.chapterName: Nature and Scope of Business Economics
questions.source: ICAI Business Economics study material – Unit 1: Nature and Scope of Business Economics

questions.text: A student gives up a job paying ₹15,000 per month to study full time. For her, the ₹15,000 forgone each month is an example of:
questions.explanation: Income forgone from the next best alternative is the opportunity cost of studying.
questions.chapterName: Nature and Scope of Business Economics
questions.source: ICAI Business Economics study material – Unit 1: Nature and Scope of Business Economics

questions.text: Under the incremental principle, a decision is profitable if:
options: it raises revenue by more than it raises costs
it raises revenue even if costs rise by more
it lowers the cost of one department only
questions.explanation: Incremental revenue must exceed incremental cost for profit to rise.
questions.chapterName: Nature and Scope of Business Economics
questions.source: ICAI Business Economics study material – Unit 1: Nature and Scope of Business Economics

questions.text: In the traditional classification, the reward for entrepreneurship is:
questions.explanation: Rent rewards land, wages labour, interest capital and profit the entrepreneur.
questions.chapterName: Nature and Scope of Business Economics
questions.source: ICAI Business Economics study material – Unit 1: Nature and Scope of Business Economics

questions.text: A point lying outside the existing production possibility curve is:
options: unattainable with the given resources and technology
a point of constant opportunity cost
questions.explanation: Only an increase in resources or better technology can make an outside point attainable.
questions.chapterName: Nature and Scope of Business Economics
questions.source: ICAI Business Economics study material – Unit 1: Nature and Scope of Business Economics

questions.text: The opportunity cost of a decision is:
options: the value of the next best alternative forgone
the cost incurred in the past
the money actually paid for the chosen option
the sum of the values of all alternatives
questions.explanation: Because resources have alternative uses, the real cost of any choice is the best alternative given up.
questions.chapterName: Nature and Scope of Business Economics
questions.source: ICAI Business Economics study material – Unit 1: Nature and Scope of Business Economics

questions.text: Which of the following is a macroeconomic issue?
options: Determination of the general price level
The output decision of a single firm
The price of a single brand of tea
The demand of one household for milk
questions.explanation: Macroeconomics studies aggregates such as the general price level, national income and total employment.
questions.chapterName: Nature and Scope of Business Economics
questions.source: ICAI Business Economics study material – Unit 1: Nature and Scope of Business Economics

questions.text: "Ceteris paribus" in economic analysis means:
questions.explanation: It isolates the effect of one variable by assuming all others unchanged.
questions.chapterName: Nature and Scope of Business Economics
questions.source: ICAI Business Economics study material – Unit 1: Nature and Scope of Business Economics

questions.text: Which of the following is a capital good?
options: A television bought for home use
A lathe machine used in a factory
questions.explanation: Capital goods are used to produce other goods; the others are consumer goods or services.
questions.chapterName: Nature and Scope of Business Economics
questions.source: ICAI Business Economics study material – Unit 1: Nature and Scope of Business Economics

questions.text: Business economics is best described as:
options: the application of economic theory and analysis to business decision-making
a branch of law relating to commerce
the study of only national income
questions.explanation: Business (managerial) economics bridges economic theory and business practice to support decisions.
questions.chapterName: Nature and Scope of Business Economics
questions.source: ICAI Business Economics study material – Unit 1: Nature and Scope of Business Economics

questions.text: Which of the following is NOT one of the central problems of an economy?
questions.explanation: The central problems are what, how and for whom to produce. Taxation is a policy instrument, not a central problem.

questions.source: ICAI Business Economics study material – Unit 1: Nature and Scope of Business Economics

questions.text: An economy moves along its production possibility curve from (20 units of X, 60 units of Y) to (30 units of X, 35 units of Y). The opportunity cost of one additional unit of X is:
questions.explanation: Increase in X = 10; sacrifice of Y = 25. Opportunity cost of 1 unit of X = 25/10 = 2.5 units of Y.
questions.formula: Opportunity cost of X = Loss of Y ÷ Gain in X

questions.text: Which sequence correctly represents the phases of a business cycle?
questions.explanation: After a trough the economy expands to a peak, then contracts to a new trough.
questions.source: ICAI Business Economics study material – Unit 5: Business Cycles

questions.text: Which of the following is NOT a phase of a business cycle?
questions.explanation: Devaluation is an exchange-rate policy, not a phase.
questions.source: ICAI Business Economics study material – Unit 5: Business Cycles

questions.text: A recession is generally characterised by:
questions.explanation: Contraction lowers demand, output and jobs.
questions.source: ICAI Business Economics study material – Unit 5: Business Cycles

questions.text: Business cycles are fluctuations in:
options: aggregate economic activity such as output, employment and income
the price of a single commodity
questions.explanation: They concern economy-wide activity.
questions.source: ICAI Business Economics study material – Unit 5: Business Cycles

questions.text: Which of the following is a feature of a trough?
options: Highest level of prices and output
Lowest level of output and employment, with idle capacity
questions.explanation: At the trough, the economy is at its weakest.
questions.source: ICAI Business Economics study material – Unit 5: Business Cycles

questions.text: The highest point of a business cycle is called the:
questions.explanation: At the peak, activity is at its maximum before turning down.
questions.source: ICAI Business Economics study material – Unit 5: Business Cycles

questions.text: Which action is most likely for firms in the recovery phase?
options: Increase production and hiring as demand revives
questions.explanation: Revival in demand encourages higher output and employment.
questions.source: ICAI Business Economics study material – Unit 5: Business Cycles

questions.text: Which of the following typically characterises the expansion/boom phase?
options: Rising output, employment and investment with rising prices
questions.explanation: Growing demand pulls up output, jobs and eventually prices.
questions.source: ICAI Business Economics study material – Unit 5: Business Cycles

questions.text: Business cycles are:
questions.explanation: They repeat but vary in duration and intensity.
questions.source: ICAI Business Economics study material – Unit 5: Business Cycles

questions.text: The lowest point of a business cycle is called the:
questions.explanation: Output and employment are at their lowest before recovery begins.
questions.source: ICAI Business Economics study material – Unit 5: Business Cycles

questions.text: A fall in aggregate demand leading firms to cut production and employment signals movement into:
questions.explanation: Falling demand reduces output and jobs.
questions.source: ICAI Business Economics study material – Unit 5: Business Cycles

questions.text: The Keynesian explanation attributes business cycles mainly to fluctuations in:
questions.explanation: Swings in consumption and investment demand drive output fluctuations.
questions.source: ICAI Business Economics study material – Unit 5: Business Cycles

options: It is a severe and prolonged downturn with very high unemployment and low demand
It is a period of full employment
It is a short-lived mild slowdown
It is the same as the peak
questions.explanation: Depression is the extreme form of contraction.
